memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But Moses said, "Here I am among six hundred thousand men on foot, and you say, 'I will give them meat to eat for a whole month!' Would they have enough if flocks and herds were slaughtered for them? Would they have enough if all the fish in the sea were caught for them?" The Lord answered Moses, "Is the Lord's arm too short? Now you will see whether or not what I say will come true for you." — Num 11:21-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Even Moses, who had watched the Red Sea split and manna fall daily, stumbles here. Faced with feeding six hundred thousand men meat for a month, he does the math and concludes it is impossible. His faith, so strong in some moments, wobbles when the problem seems too large.

How gently God answers: "Is the Lord's arm too short?" It is one of the most quietly powerful questions in the Bible. God does not scold Moses for his doubt; He simply reminds him who He is. The One who made the seas and stars is not stretched thin by any need we bring Him.

We are so much like Moses. We believe God for the small things, then quietly assume the big things are beyond even Him. We calculate our resources — our money, our energy, our options — and decide the situation is hopeless. But God's power is not limited by our arithmetic.

Whatever impossible thing you are staring at today, hear the same question spoken to you: "Is the Lord's arm too short?" The God who raised Jesus from the dead is not short of power for your situation. Your part is not to figure out how; your part is to trust the One who can.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What situation feels too big even for God to handle?
2. Where have you limited God by your own calculations?
3. How does the resurrection of Jesus reassure you of God's power?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for shrinking You down to the size of my resources. You are the God of the impossible, whose arm is never too short. Help me to trust Your power over my problems. Amen.
